column1: Zero-inflated Stochastic Volatility Model for Disaggregated Inflation Data with Exact Zeros

The thesis titled Zero-inflated stochastic volatility model for disaggregated inflation data with exact zeros by Geonhee Han and Kaoru Irie addresses the challenge of modeling disaggregated Consumer Price Index (CPI) data  which often includes frequent instances of exact zero price changes due to measurement errors. Traditional stochastic volatility models  typically used for aggregate inflation measures  do not account for these exact zeros  which are more prevalent in disaggregated data. The authors propose a zero-inflated stochastic volatility model tailored for non-stationary  real-valued multivariate time-series data with exact zeros. This model employs a Bayesian dynamic generalized linear model to jointly specify the dynamic zero-generating process  utilizing a custom Gibbs sampler with Pólya-Gamma augmentation for efficient computation.

The model is applied to disaggregated CPI data from the US  UK  Germany  and Japan  demonstrating that it provides more accurate and informative estimates of time-varying trends and volatility compared to traditional models. The zero-inflated model also shows improved performance in out-of-sample forecasting  particularly in scenarios with prevalent zero-inflation. The study highlights the limitations of conventional state-space models  which assume continuous responses and may produce biased estimates in the presence of zeros  thus underscoring the need for models that can handle zero-inflation in economic datasets.

The authors discuss the occurrence of exact zeros in economic data  such as stocks with low trading volumes or private real estate investment trusts  where data points are often imputed using the most recent available value. These zeros can lead to biased location estimates and underestimated variance in conventional models  which is problematic for accurately estimating time-varying means or volatilities. The study also references macroeconomic literature that attributes price staleness to time- and state-dependent firm-level price adjustment behaviors.

Despite the prevalence of zero-inflation  existing stochastic volatility models for trend-inflation have largely ignored this phenomenon  focusing instead on aggregate inflation data where price staleness is less pronounced. The authors note that while some models account for zero-inflation or disaggregate measures  they often lack the capability to estimate trends and volatilities. The proposed zero-inflated model addresses this gap by incorporating a latent dynamic logistic model to account for heterogeneous cross-sectional propensity  temporal persistence  and cross-correlation in zeros.

The study contributes to the literature by developing a zero-inflated multivariate stochastic volatility model that generalizes the unobserved components stochastic volatility (UC)SV model. This model explicitly specifies the exact-zero generating process alongside the (UC)SV-driven nonzero generating process  forming a joint Bayesian model based on the dynamic generalized linear model (DGLM). The approach allows for a more accurate representation of disaggregated CPI data  providing valuable insights for policymakers and financial institutions in shaping policy and financing strategies.
